title: What are arrays, strings?
subStepTitle: Things to Know in C++/Java/Python or any language
subcategory: Things to Know in C++/Java/Python or any language
problemStatement: Arrays/strings are contiguous sequences with O(1) index access — the default DSA canvas.
intuition: Index → value in O(1). Python strings are immutable — concat in a loop is a hidden O(n²) TLE trap. Use lists + join.

approaches.title: Indexing, mutability, building strings
approaches.idea: list for mutable sequences; build strings with join.
approaches.code:
a = [3, 1, 4]
a[0] = 2
s = "ada"
chars = list(s)
chars[0] = "A"
s2 = "".join(chars)

parts = []
for ch in "abc":
    parts.append(ch)
print("".join(parts))  # O(n)
limitations: Naive string += in a loop → O(n²) → TLE for n~1e5

complexity.space: O(1) extra for scans; O(n) for copies

patternRecognition: Contiguous → two pointers / sliding window / prefix sums
interviewInsight: Random vs sequential access tradeoffs should be automatic.
